the use of a hybrid of binary cross-entropy and Jaccard Loss, the use of a coarse map initialization, and the use of an ensemble of varied backbone networks in a U-net architecture is best at the single view semantic 3D challenge.

the use of an ensemble of varied U Net backbones, specific band combination from the multispectral imagery and a hybrid loss function are best suited for semantic segmentation, while a coarse map initialization is best for height prediction.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel deep learning architecture for single view semantic 3D reconstruction from satellite imagery.
the development of a robust and accurate model to predict semantic labels as well as the height estimation from a single view satellite imagery.
the development of a novel ensemble U Net architecture for semantic segmentation and height estimation using multi-spectral data from the single view imagery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed ensemble architecture, along with the use of a hybrid of binary cross-entropy and Jaccard losses for the semantic labels and the coarse map initialization, proved to be the best combination for this particular challenge task.
the ensemble of varied backbones, along with the use of a coarse map initialization, is best at both the semantic segmentation and normalized height prediction tasks.
the ensemble of U Nets, with a hybrid loss function and a coarse map initialization is a good approach towards semantic segmentation and height estimation from single view imagery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of the coarse height map initialization to a U Net architecture for height estimation, is a good way to improve the convergence and the accuracy of the height prediction.
the ensemble of U N et backbones with a hybrid loss function and the use of a coarse map initialization is a good choice for the task of semantic and height estimation from a single view.

we have shown that the use of a few varied backbone networks in an ensemble, along with the use of hybrid losses, and the addition of a global mean map initialization, is best for the semantic and height estimation tasks in the Single View Semantic 3D Track of the GRSS 2020 Data Fusion Contest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of a U Net with an ensemble of backbones, with a specific band combination, and the use of a coarse map initialization, is best for semantic and height prediction tasks.
a simple U Net architecture with few variations in backbone can perform well in both semantic segmentation and normalized height prediction tasks, with a simple ensemble of models.
a simple ensemble of a few backbones, with a coarse map initialization for height prediction, can outperform a more complex architecture.
